truth_states: FACT = verified in source at the cited line; UPSTREAM = bundled-doc claim, drift-prone; INFERENCE = producer reasoning, labeled

entries.name: Static provider catalog registry (10 typed collections, 356 records)
entries.purpose: Canonical static registry of provider metadata (id, alias, auth type, icons, hints, serviceKinds) in 10 collections — noauth 13, oauth 25, web-cookie 35, local 14, search 16, audio 12, upstream-proxy 2, cloud-agent 3, system 1, apikey 235; 356 unique ids, zero duplicates [FACT, counted deterministically from source]; grouped into 9 dashboard categories by STATIC_PROVIDER_CATALOG_GROUPS (system excluded).
entries.risk_class: low — static in-repo data literal; wrong entries degrade display/routing metadata but hold no credentials
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — enumerate collections, assert 356 unique ids and per-category counts; routed — resolve each id via resolveStaticProviderCatalogEntry (catalog.ts:195) and assert category round-trip; regression — doc counts (353/354) must NOT be asserted, source counts are the truth
entries.rollback_or_disable: Pure data; removing a record drops it from dashboard/catalog resolution (catalog.ts:195-212). No runtime toggle found; revert = git-level change [INFERENCE: no feature flag for registry content found in source]

entries.name: Runtime chat-model provider REGISTRY (272 entries)
entries.purpose: Runtime per-provider configuration (format, baseUrl(s), headers, OAuth, models, alternateFormats) consumed by executors and URL builders; generateLegacyProviders() (providerRegistry.ts:34) re-projects it to the legacy PROVIDERS shape for backward compatibility. 272 plain key:provider entries, no spreads (index.ts lines 274-547) [FACT].
entries.risk_class: medium — wrong baseUrl/headers misroutes live traffic or leaks keys to the wrong upstream (see CAP-P2-004 guard history)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — count REGISTRY keys (expect 272), spot-resolve entries through getRegistryEntry; routed — per-provider request-shape golden tests (tests/unit/executor-map-golden.test.ts pattern); negative — unknown provider id must not resolve
entries.rollback_or_disable: Per-entry removal from the object literal; consumers fall back to DefaultExecutor+OpenAI-compatible assumptions only when an entry exists — deleting an entry changes dispatch, so revert is source-level

entries.name: ExecutorRegistry — lazy provider-executor dispatch
entries.purpose: Runtime alias→executor map; 144 aliases declared with lazy module loaders (119 dynamic imports) registering at boot and materializing on first use (#11220); getExecutor() (index.ts:244) resolves specialized executors, hard-blocks cloud-agent-only providers (jules, index.ts:231) and all search providers (derived set, index.ts:242) with HTTP 400, then falls back to DefaultExecutor.
entries.risk_class: high — dispatch seam for all upstream traffic; alias/dup registration throws at boot, and mis-resolution historically routed keys to the wrong host (#6699 comment, index.ts)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — golden snapshot tests/unit/executor-map-golden.test.ts pins alias keys/order/instances; negative — jules and any SEARCH_PROVIDERS key must throw 400 on chat path; routed — alias resolution returns the same class as canonical id
entries.rollback_or_disable: Aliases are removable from the lazyExecutors table (index.ts:30); duplicate-alias throw (registry.ts:22) prevents shadowing; no runtime disable flag found

entries.name: DefaultExecutor — OpenAI-compatible fallback dispatch
entries.purpose: Generic executor for any provider without a specialized class: resolves URL/headers from the REGISTRY/PROVIDERS config, applies per-provider URL normalizers (Azure, watsonx, OCI, SAP, Databricks, Snowflake, GigaChat), OAuth token refresh, Claude-Code-compatible headers, and param stripping — the OpenAI-compatible passthrough path.
entries.risk_class: high — silent fall-through to PROVIDERS.openai with the user's real key is the documented failure mode (#6699 comment, executors/index.ts); guards exist only for cloud-agent and search providers
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — unknown-but-registered provider hits its configured baseUrl (mock upstream), never api.openai.com; negative — unconfigured provider must not receive another provider's credentials; persistence — per-provider defaultCache (index.ts:261) isolation
entries.rollback_or_disable: Per-provider specialized executor registration overrides the fallback; no global kill-switch for the fallback itself found in source

entries.name: Specialized provider executor classes (144 aliases / 119 modules)
entries.purpose: Provider-specific HTTP dispatch classes for native/quirky upstreams — cloud (bedrock, vertex, azure-openai), web-session (claude-web, gemini-web, chatgpt-web, deepseek-web), CLI/app bridges (auggie, codex-app-server, zcode, devin-cli), and regional providers — each overriding BaseExecutor request/response behavior.
entries.risk_class: medium — per-provider wire behavior incl. cookie/session reuse and fingerprinting; defects are provider-scoped, not systemic
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — per-executor contract tests against recorded upstream fixtures (tests/fixtures/* pattern); negative — malformed upstream SSE must surface as provider error, not silent fallback
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the alias from lazyExecutors (index.ts:30) → provider drops to DefaultExecutor or 400 guard; per-connection disable via dashboard provider toggle [INFERENCE: connection-level disable path not traced this partition]

entries.name: TranslatorRegistry — hub-and-spoke format translation engine
entries.purpose: Pair-keyed ('from:to') request/response translator maps with side-effect bootstrap registration (9 request + 9 response modules); translateRequest/translateResponse use the direct pair or fall back to hub-and-spoke via OpenAI (index.ts:456, 817); 9 format identifiers (FORMATS, formats.ts:2): openai, openai-responses, openai-response (legacy alias), claude, gemini, codex, antigravity, kiro, cursor.
entries.risk_class: medium — semantic drift in translation corrupts payloads silently; the frozen acceptance corpus exists to catch it (tests/fixtures/translation/*)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — pair registry lookups for all registered keys; routed — fixture-based translation goldens (tests/fixtures/translation/); negative — unregistered pair must use the OpenAI hub, never invent a mapping
entries.rollback_or_disable: needsTranslation (index.ts:864) short-circuits same-format traffic; removing a bootstrap import unregisters that pair — translation then falls through the hub [INFERENCE: no runtime translation kill-switch found]

entries.name: OpenAI↔Claude translation adapters
entries.purpose: Bidirectional request and streaming-response translation between OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages formats, incl. thinking blocks, tool calls, and cache-control handling (helpers/claudeHelper.ts).
entries.risk_class: medium — Anthropic-native semantics (thinking, tool_use) can be lossy in translation; errors are per-request
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — fixture goldens for both directions incl. streaming chunks and tool_use; negative — unsupported params stripped per STRIP_RULES, not silently passed
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unregister via bootstrap.ts import removal; native Claude-format clients can bypass by targeting a claude-format provider directly

entries.name: OpenAI↔Gemini translation adapters
entries.purpose: Bidirectional OpenAI Chat Completions ↔ Google Gemini generateContent translation, incl. SSE response conversion (response/openai-to-gemini-sse.ts) and Gemini tool-schema sanitizing (helpers/geminiToolsSanitizer.ts).
entries.risk_class: medium — schema coercion for Gemini's stricter function-declaration format can drop tool fields
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — fixture goldens incl. malformed-function-call recovery (tests/fixtures/translation/gemini-malformed-*); negative — invalid schema must be coerced or rejected, never upstreamed raw
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unregister via bootstrap.ts import removal; hub fallback covers indirect paths

entries.name: Claude↔Gemini direct translation adapters
entries.purpose: Direct Claude→Gemini request and Gemini→Claude response translation (Antigravity→Claude shares the gemini→claude response fn, registered at :368) so Anthropic-format clients can front Gemini upstreams without a double hop through OpenAI format.
entries.risk_class: medium — double-translation semantics (thinking/config mapping) are the most drift-prone of the registered pairs
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — Claude-format request to a Gemini upstream round-trip fixture; negative — hub fallback must NOT engage for this pair (direct registration exists)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unregister via bootstrap.ts; hub-and-spoke via OpenAI then covers the path automatically

entries.name: OpenAI Responses API adapters + Responses transformer
entries.purpose: Bidirectional Chat Completions ↔ Responses API translation (request/response pairs registered both ways), plus the streaming responsesTransformer converting Chat Completions SSE into Responses API SSE for Codex-style clients; legacy 'openai-response' identifier normalized to 'openai-responses' at streamPayloadCollector.ts:72.
entries.risk_class: medium — reasoning/state item semantics (reasoning replay, store markers) are subtle; corruption affects Codex-class clients
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — Responses↔Chat round-trip fixtures incl. streaming item lifecycle; negative — corrupted request_id stripping (transformer threshold 200 chars) must not alter valid payloads
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unregister pairs via bootstrap.ts; transformer is engaged only for Responses-format client paths [INFERENCE: engagement condition not fully traced this partition]

entries.name: IDE/agent-format adapters (Kiro, Cursor, Antigravity)
entries.purpose: Translation pairs for vendor IDE/agent wire formats: openai→kiro, kiro→openai, openai→cursor, cursor→openai, antigravity→openai (request), openai→antigravity (request at openai-to-gemini.ts:850 and response at openai-to-antigravity.ts:145) — letting those client ecosystems ride the OpenAI hub.
entries.risk_class: medium — vendor-format drift tracks external IDE releases; failures are ecosystem-scoped
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — per-format fixture round-trips; negative — unregistered direction must hub-fallback or error, never passthrough
entries.rollback_or_disable: Unregister via bootstrap.ts import removal

entries.name: Parameter-support stripping (STRIP_RULES)
entries.purpose: stripUnsupportedParams() removes request parameters a target provider does not support, driven by a declarative STRIP_RULES table (exported for tests at :251); invoked in the DefaultExecutor dispatch path.
entries.risk_class: medium — over-stripping silently degrades requests (dropped temperature/tools); under-stripping causes upstream 400s
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — rule-table unit tests against __STRIP_RULES_FOR_TEST; routed — request to a restricted provider asserts stripped fields absent upstream
entries.rollback_or_disable: Rules are data rows in STRIP_RULES; removal restores passthrough for that param/provider pair

entries.name: Alternate-format protocol switch per connection
entries.purpose: Providers may declare alternate wire protocols on the same host (e.g. OpenAI /v1/chat/completions and Anthropic /anthropic/v1/messages); the choice lives per-connection in providerSpecificData.targetFormat and must match a declared alternative, else the default format is used (alternateFormats.ts header comment).
entries.risk_class: medium — per-connection protocol selection swaps URL+auth headers; a bad match sends credentials under the wrong auth scheme
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — switch a connection's targetFormat and assert URL/header/auth change; negative — undeclared targetFormat must fall back to default, never produce orphaned URL/auth
entries.rollback_or_disable: Reset the connection's providerSpecificData.targetFormat to the default format

entries.name: Provider connection persistence (SQLite provider_connections)
entries.purpose: CRUD + backoff/error state for user-configured provider connections (credentials references, priority, testStatus, providerSpecificData) in the SQLite layer; createProviderConnection at :444, updateProviderConnection at :902, cleanupProviderConnections at :1099.
entries.risk_class: high — connection rows carry API keys/tokens (secret-handling surface) and drive live routing
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: persistence — create/read/update/delete round-trip incl. restart survival; negative — secret values must never appear in logs/error strings [INFERENCE: encryption verified by P5, not this partition]
entries.rollback_or_disable: DELETE via management API (route.ts:406) removes connections; DB backup/restore per P5 runbooks

entries.name: OAuth provider flows (25 oauth-catalog providers)
entries.purpose: OAuth authorization flow for catalog OAuth providers (claude, codex, github, cursor, kiro, gemini-business...): getProvider (:117) resolves provider config, generateAuthData (:133) builds auth URLs/state; token refresh consumed by executors via services/tokenRefresh.
entries.risk_class: high — handles user OAuth tokens and redirect URIs; misconfiguration exposes tokens or breaks auth silently
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — full auth-code flow against a loopback mock IdP; negative — state/nonce mismatch must abort; persistence — refresh survives restart
entries.rollback_or_disable: OAuth providers are optional; removing the connection disables the flow. No global OAuth kill-switch found

entries.name: Provider management API + key validation
entries.purpose: Dashboard/management CRUD for providers and connections (GET :49, POST :105, PATCH :349, DELETE :406) with live key validation via validateProviderApiKey (validation.ts:176) and per-provider model listing under /api/v1/providers/[provider]/*.
entries.risk_class: high — management endpoints mutate credential-bearing configuration; authN/authZ on these routes is P4 scope, flagged here as the coupling point
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — CRUD round-trip via API with auth enforced (P4 contract); negative — unauthenticated request must 401/403; routed — validateProviderApiKey against mock upstream
entries.rollback_or_disable: Routes are inherent to the dashboard; operator-level disable = do not expose management plane beyond the LAN boundary (HX exposure rule)

entries.name: Compatible provider nodes (operator-added OpenAI/Anthropic/CC-compatible endpoints)
entries.purpose: Operator-defined compatible endpoints (openai-compatible / anthropic-compatible / claude-code-compatible) resolved through resolveCompatibleProviderCatalogEntry (catalog.ts:222) — the mechanism by which arbitrary LAN/self-hosted endpoints (e.g. an HX Ollama OpenAI-compatible server) become routable providers.
entries.risk_class: medium — arbitrary baseUrl egress (SSRF-adjacent; private-host handling via isPrivateHost import at providerRegistry.ts:16); no upstream ToS risk for LAN endpoints
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — add a compatible node pointing at a mock LAN endpoint, assert chat round-trip; negative — private-host/egress rules per P4 must hold
entries.rollback_or_disable: Delete the provider node (management API DELETE); traffic stops immediately

entries.name: Local providers collection (ollama-local, lm-studio, vllm, llama-cpp + 10 more)
entries.purpose: First-class catalog for 14 local inference servers (ollama-local at local.ts:32, lm-studio, vllm, llama-cpp, triton, docker-model-runner, xinference, oobabooga, mlx-*, comfyui, sdwebui, lemonade, llamafile) with dedicated model-listing support (open-sse/config/ollamaModels.ts).
entries.risk_class: low — loopback/LAN endpoints, no external egress or ToS exposure; availability is the main failure mode
dependencies: CAP-P2-017 compatible nodes for custom locals
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: routed — ollama-local chat + model listing against a live/mock Ollama; negative — server down must trip provider health, not hang requests
entries.rollback_or_disable: Remove the connection or leave the provider unconfigured; locals are inert without a reachable server

entries.name: Service-kind provider registries (search/audio/image/video/embedding/moderation/ocr/rerank/upscale/music)
entries.purpose: Non-chat capability registries: searchRegistry (19 providers, SEARCH_PROVIDERS at :38 — also the source of the chat-path 400 guard), plus audio, image, video, embedding, moderation, ocr, rerank, upscale, music registries defining per-kind provider configs and endpoints.
entries.risk_class: medium — search keys historically leakable to OpenAI endpoint (#10274 comment, executors/index.ts) before the derived guard; per-kind registries are data, defects are kind-scoped
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: direct — registry key counts (search=19); negative — every SEARCH_PROVIDERS key must 400 on chat completions; routed — /v1/search round-trip per provider config
entries.rollback_or_disable: Registries are data; unused kinds are inert. Guard set auto-derives, so removing a search provider shrinks the guard consistently

entries.name: Web-cookie providers + web session contract (35 providers)
entries.purpose: Browser-session/cookie-authenticated providers (claude-web, chatgpt-web, gemini-web, grok-web, deepseek-web...) governed by a versioned WEB_SESSION_CONTRACT (webSessionContract.ts:7) and dedicated web executors; subscription-risk flagged in catalog metadata (riskNoticeVariant).
entries.risk_class: high — rides consumer web sessions against upstream ToS (subscription-risk class in source); session theft or upstream ban are the documented-shaped failures
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: contract — buildWebSessionContract validates provider set; routed — recorded-fixture web executor behavior only (no live third-party session use without owner approval)
entries.rollback_or_disable: Web providers require an imported session to function; absent sessions they are inert. Delete connection/session to disable

entries.name: Cloud-agent providers (jules, devin, codex-cloud task APIs)
entries.purpose: Three cloud-agent task-API providers (jules :6, devin :16, plus codex-cloud family) exposed through the Cloud Agents task API rather than chat completions; chat path hard-blocked by the CHAT_UNSUPPORTED_CLOUD_AGENT_PROVIDERS guard (executors/index.ts:231).
entries.risk_class: high — agent-surface class: delegates task execution to external cloud agents; HX policy keeps agent-like surfaces disabled by default
dependencies: Cloud Agents task API surface (P7 scope)
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: negative — chat completion to jules must return 400 with the cloud-agent message; contract — task-API surface assessed under P7 before any enablement
entries.rollback_or_disable: Disabled by construction for chat; enablement of the task API is a separate owner decision

entries.name: Upstream-proxy embedded services + provider plugin seam (cliproxyapi, 9router)
entries.purpose: Two embedded upstream-proxy providers (cliproxyapi, 9router — 9router marked isEmbeddedService with riskNoticeVariant 'embedded-service') plus the ServiceProviderPlugin registry (registry.ts:20, currently typed Record<'9router',...> deliberately narrow) and the provider-plugin manifest generator (providerPluginManifest.ts) — the seam toward host.registerProvider-style extensibility.
entries.risk_class: high — spawns/manages child processes and embedded services (spawnArgs, ports, health loops); process-spawning surfaces are disabled-by-default per HX policy
dependencies: CAP-P2-003 executor entries for cliproxyapi/9router aliases
entries.test_contract: Layer-N: contract — plugin registry shape and manifest generation from REGISTRY; negative — no child process may spawn without an explicit operator action [INFERENCE: spawn trigger path not traced this partition]
entries.rollback_or_disable: Embedded services run only when installed/enabled by the operator; uninstall/disable via the services surface. Plugin seam is inert with a single registered entry

entries.name: ATEM/native protocol adapter
entries.purpose: Work order asks for an 'ATEM/native' protocol adapter. Searched: case-sensitive whole-word 'ATEM' across src/, open-sse/, packages/, docs/, config/ (grep -rInw) — zero matches; case-insensitive 'atem' sweep returns only substring noise (i18n strings, unrelated identifiers). No ATEM protocol, adapter, or format identifier exists in the corpus. The native (non-OpenAI) protocol paths that DO exist are claude, gemini, codex, antigravity, kiro, cursor (FORMATS, formats.ts:2) covered by CAP-P2-006/007/008/009/010/011.
entries.risk_class: low — absence verified; no capability to assess
entries.test_contract: N/A — nothing to prove; re-run the same grep on any future snapshot to confirm continued absence
